newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand shrugged off a strong dollar to close up on the U.S. unit and stormed ahead on the crosses, hitting a six-month high against the mark and five-week high against sterling.

The currency ended the day at 4.6400/6450 on the dollar from 4.6425/6475 at the Friday close. On the crosses, it was last six-and-a-half cents stronger at 7.7108/7238 on sterling from 7.7758/7888 late on Friday, while on the mark it was trading at 0.3496/3502 from 0.3458/3463 late Friday.
Forex traders said exporter and offshore dollars had flowed into the market throughout the day.
"The guys are nervous of holding long dollar positions over long periods...it's becoming too expensive," a trader at a leading local bank told Reuters.
"We saw quite a bit of offshore interest to sell dollars and local importer demand for dollars appears to have dried up...they're not covering anymore," she added.

Other forex traders said the rand had ignored a strong dollar in European trade where the U.S. unit climbed to new multi-year highs against the mark, yen and Swiss franc with little seen standing in its way.
The currency market continued to be buoyed by a bullish mood and the perception was that the rand would stabilise as the year progressed, traders said.
One expected the rand to test the lower 4.60 levels in the course of the week.
"It's possible that we will see a test of 4.62 to 4.63 on the dollar later in the week at which point there could be a small correction," the trader said.

Long bonds had a relatively steady day with the yield on government's benchmark R150 bond last at 15.59 percent from 15.57 percent late on Friday after briefly moving above 15.60 percent during the morning.
Bond traders said yields broke through the 15.60 percent level but soon met resistance at 15.65 percent -- a technical support level.
"What we saw today was a bit of a retracement in a bull trend but there was little institutional interest in the market," a senior trader said.
The market was hampered by a lack of fresh economic and political news and a federal holiday in the U.S. where the Treasury market was closed for the day.
The short-term outlook for the local bond market remained bullish with 15.30 percent in sight on the downside, traders said.
A high money market shortage above ten billion rand despite expectations of a drop after December was not too much of a worry as dealers expected foreign inflows to show up soon.
South Africa's money market shortage dipped marginally to 10.403 billion rand on Saturday from Friday's 10.488 billion rand, the Reserve Bank said.
Leading banks quoted their three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.25-17.50 percent while 90-day BA rates were also unchanged at 16.60-16.85 percent.
Foreigners were big net buyers of 709.33 million rand worth of South African bonds last week, latest Bond Exchange of South Africa figures showed.
On Friday, foreigners bought a net 142.28 million rands worth of South African bonds after selling 68.35 million rands on Thursday, the exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 7.07 million rand on Friday from 36.42 million rand on Thursday -- a settlement date.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
